subject: Ephemeral cache & revenue-share framework for Pinecone S3-backed routing
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@clearcloud.consulting>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: ephemeral cache revenue-share for S3-backed fallthrough

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the call last week. As discussed, Pinecone is interested in a tighter commercial and operational agreement for a hybrid routing mode where Pinecone handles hot indexes and Redwood routes cold/fallthrough reads to S3-backed embeddings. The ask from our GTM team is a simple, predictable rev-share on storage egress and index request volume when the traffic is routed through a Pinecone-managed cache layer.

High-level items we think should be in scope:
- revenue-share % on index request volume (read-heavy queries) routed to Pinecone cache
- clear SLOs for TTL/eviction and cold-read latency targets
- attribution signal (request headers or route tags) so usage splits are auditable
- a lightweight onboarding checklist for customer enablement and ops playbook

I've attached a short term sheet to start (see "ephemeral cache term sheet"). Clara from ClearCloud is CC'd — they'll run an independent ops review and can suggest sane defaults.

Would you be open to a 30-min alignment session later this week to map cost splits and the minimal engineering changes required?

— Alex
Director, Alliances | Pinecone

Attachment: 20261124-ephemeral-cache-term-sheet-draft.pdf (1 page)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>, Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@clearcloud.consulting>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: ephemeral cache revenue-share for S3-backed fallthrough

Alex / Clara —

Thanks for the draft and for outlining the scoping. Vanessa and Ben are looped for commercial and ops sizing. Quick thoughts from Redwood:

- We like a simple per-request rev-share + a small per-GB egress for cold reads routed through your cache. Exact bands depend on percent cache-hit we can guarantee.
- We will need explicit attribution headers (we can add X-Redwood-Route: pinecone_hotbounce) so billing reconciliation is straightforward.
- SLOs: 95th p95 cold-read under 400ms and eviction TTL options (30m / 2h / 24h) — we can be flexible but need clear observability hooks.

Can Ben build a quick cost model to show break-even points at 5k/25k/100k qps? Vanessa — if we agree on the framework, I'd like us to propose a pilot customer (low risk) and a checklist for compliance (data residency, audit logs).

I can do a 30-min sync Thurs 11/26 11am PT or Fri 11/27 2pm PT — which works for you?

— Hannah
Sr. Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Proposal: ephemeral cache revenue-share for S3-backed fallthrough

Hannah / Vanessa —

I've attached a quick cost model and three scenarios (conservative / typical / aggressive) in the spreadsheet. Key assumptions called out on tab 1. Topline: at cache-hit > 70% rev-share of 8-12% on index request revenue looks commercially viable for Redwood and keeps customer unit-costs down. Below 40% hit rates the economics don't make sense unless we add a minimum monthly guarantee.

Operational asks from my side:
- a simple header for attribution as Hannah suggested; we can also emit a usage tag in our tracing pipeline to validate on both sides.
- weekly ledger export (CSV) that both sides reconcile for pilot months.
- a defined escalation matrix for any degradation of cold-read latency.

I've flagged the cells where MX costs change materially. Will be on the review call tomorrow.

Attachment: 20261126-internal-cost-model.xlsx

— Ben
Partner Ops Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@clearcloud.consulting>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: ephemeral cache revenue-share for S3-backed fallthrough

Folks —

I ran an ops sanity check on the term sheet. Two operational risk items to highlight:
1) Attribution drift when customers use multi-path routing (app-managed vs platform-managed). Recommend adding a signed request token to validate source of truth.
2) S3 egress billing granularity — many providers bill at a bucket level which can make per-customer splits noisy. Suggest a monthly reconciliation and a small buffer credit for noisy months.

Suggested pilot checklist (short):
- instrument X-Redwood-Route header + signed token
- pilot customer (we recommend Acme Retail as they've low PII risk)
- define ledger format and weekly export cadence
- run a 48-hour soak to validate hit-rate assumptions

Happy to present the checklist on the call and help draft pilot runbook.

— Clara
Principal, ClearCloud Consulting

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@pinecone.io>, Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@clearcloud.consulting>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, ops@acme-storage.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: ephemeral cache revenue-share for S3-backed fallthrough

Thanks everyone — productive thread. Quick decisions and next steps: 

Decisions:
- Pilot model: 10% rev-share on index request revenue when cache-hit >= 65%. Below 65% we will fallback to a minimum monthly guarantee of $2,500 for pilot customers.
- Observability: Redwood to add X-Redwood-Route and signed token; Pinecone to accept token and emit request id for reconciliation.
- SLOs: cold-read p95 <= 400ms for pilot; escalation matrix documented in runbook.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Ben: finalize cost model and publish break-even table to the drive link (ETA: Mon 11/30).
- Vanessa: propose one pilot customer and draft commercial one-pager for GTM (ETA: Mon 11/30).
- Clara: prepare 48-hour soak plan and runbook template (ETA: Tue 12/1).
- Alex / Pinecone: confirm acceptance of signed token approach and the weekly ledger format (ETA: Mon 11/30).

I'll book a 30-min sync Mon 11/30 10am PT to finalize pilot paperwork. Attaching the agreed term sheet stub for signatures.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20261124-ephemeral-cache-term-sheet-draft.pdf, 20261126-internal-cost-model.xlsx
